Your head is older than your feet. Right now.
Einstein predicted it in 1915. Gravity doesn't just pull on you. It slows down time.
The closer you are to the Earth, the slower your clock ticks.
In 1959, scientists at Harvard fired gamma rays down a twenty two metre tower. The light shifted, exactly as Einstein said.
In 2010, they raised a super precise clock just thirty three centimetres. It ticked faster.
By 2022, they could measure the difference across one millimetre.
Over a whole lifetime, your head ages about half a millionth of a second more than your feet.
And deep below you, the centre of the Earth is about two and a half years younger than the surface.
So every step you climb, you age a little faster. And there is no way to stop it.
